summary.text: Ripple marks are sedimentary structures that show a surface of loose sediment was stirred by water currents, waves or wind.
Ripples made by a one-way current are lopsided, with a gentle up-current slope and a steeper down-current slope, so they show which way the flow ran.
Back-and-forth wave motion usually builds roughly symmetrical ripples, though shape alone may not be enough to tell what setting they formed in.

facts.label: Current ripples
facts.value: Gentle up-current slope, steeper down-current slope

facts.label: Wave ripples
facts.value: Roughly symmetrical, with straight or gently winding crests

facts.label: Wave ripples preserved in
facts.value: Shallow seas, lakes and tidal flats

facts.label: Megaripple wavelength
facts.value: Tens of centimetres to several metres on Earth

items.prompt: An old rock shows a ripple with a gentle slope facing west and a steep slope facing east. Which way did the current run?

options.label: From west to east
From east to west
From north to south
Back and forth evenly

items.explain: Current flows up the gentle side and down the steep side, so it ran from the gentle west side toward the steep east side.

items.prompt: Small waves slosh water back and forth over a sandy lake bottom. What ripple shape is most typical there?

options.label: Lopsided, steep on the shore side
Roughly even on both sides
Flat, with no ridges at all
Lopsided, steep on the lake side

items.explain: Back-and-forth wave motion commonly builds ripples with roughly symmetrical profiles.

items.prompt: Near a beach, waves pile up and break before reaching shore. Why might the ripples they make come out lopsided?

options.label: The sand there is always too fine
Wind blows the crests flat each night
The water moves harder one way than back
Tides bury half of every ripple

items.explain: Shoaling or breaking waves can move water unequally in the two directions, which gives asymmetric wave ripples.

items.prompt: Wind blows across a patch of sand mixing fine and coarse grains. Where do the coarse grains tend to collect on the ripples?

options.label: Deep in the troughs
Spread evenly all over
Buried under the ripples
Near the ripple crests

items.explain: Bouncing grains knock sediment from troughs toward crests, and in mixed sand the coarser grains may end up concentrated near the crests.

items.prompt: A geologist finds symmetrical ripples in ancient rock. Can she be certain waves made them?

options.label: Yes, only waves make even ripples
No, other processes can make them too
Yes, wind ripples are never even
No, waves never make even ripples

items.explain: Symmetry is not unique to wave-formed ripples, and not all wave ripples are symmetrical, so shape alone does not settle it.

items.prompt: On a windy dune field, grains bouncing along keep striking the surface. What happens to the ripple pattern over time?

options.label: It stays fixed in one place
It creeps slowly upwind
It drifts slowly downwind
It sinks into the dune

items.explain: Repeated impacts move grains from troughs toward crests, which makes the ripple pattern migrate downwind.
